# Journey into Machine Learning with Sklearn and Tensorflow
## Learning Guide

---

## Course Overview

This course provides a **medium-difficulty, comprehensive introduction to machine learning** using two of the most widely-adopted Python libraries: **scikit-learn (Sklearn)** and **TensorFlow**. 

### Who This Course Is For
- Software engineers transitioning into ML/AI roles
- Data scientists strengthening their practical implementation skills
- Interview candidates preparing for ML engineering positions at tech companies
- Developers building intelligent features into production systems

### Why It Matters for Interview Prep
Machine learning has become a **core competency** for many tech roles. This course covers:
- Real-world workflows (data preprocessing → model training → evaluation)
- Both traditional ML (Sklearn) and deep learning (TensorFlow)
- Practical debugging and optimization skills
- 119 hands-on problems that mirror real interview scenarios

Mastery of Sklearn + TensorFlow demonstrates you can **implement solutions end-to-end**, not just understand theory. This is what interviewers care about.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Data Preprocessing & Feature Engineering** – Cleaning, normalization, encoding, feature scaling, and handling missing data
- **Supervised Learning Fundamentals** – Regression and classification with Sklearn (Linear/Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, SVM)
- **Unsupervised Learning** – Clustering (K-means, DBSCAN) and dimensionality reduction (PCA)
- **Model Evaluation & Selection** – Cross-validation, metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, AUC-ROC), hyperparameter tuning (Grid/Random Search)
- **Neural Networks & Deep Learning Basics** – Building sequential models with TensorFlow/Keras, activation functions, backpropagation
- **Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)** – Image classification, conv layers, pooling, transfer learning
- **Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) & LSTMs** – Time series, sequence modeling, text processing
- **Practical ML Workflow** – Train/test splits, avoiding overfitting, debugging models, deployment considerations

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–2)**

#### Step 1.1: Environment Setup & Numpy/Pandas Mastery
- Install Sklearn, TensorFlow, Jupyter
- Master NumPy arrays and Pandas DataFrames (slicing, grouping, pivoting)
- Load and explore datasets using `pandas.read_csv()`, `.describe()`, `.info()`
- **Practice tasks:** 8–10 basic data manipulation problems

#### Step 1.2: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
- Identify data types, missing values, outliers
- Visualize distributions (histograms, box plots) and relationships (scatter, correlation matrices)
- Handle missing data: imputation, deletion, forward fill
- **Practice tasks:** 10–12 EDA problems

#### Step 1.3: Data Preprocessing
- Standardization vs. Normalization (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler)
- Categorical encoding (OneHotEncoder, LabelEncoder)
- Feature scaling for Sklearn algorithms
- Train/test split best practices
- **Practice tasks:** 12–15 preprocessing problems

---

### **Phase 2: Supervised Learning with Sklearn (Weeks 3–5)**

#### Step 2.1: Regression Models
- Linear Regression: fit, predict, understand coefficients
- Polynomial Regression: degree selection, overfitting
- Ridge/Lasso regression: regularization concepts
- **Practice tasks:** 10–12 regression problems

#### Step 2.2: Classification Models
- Logistic Regression: sigmoid function, decision boundaries
- Decision Trees: splitting criteria (Gini, entropy), pruning
- Random Forests: ensemble methods, feature importance
- Support Vector Machines (SVM): kernels, margin maximization
- **Practice tasks:** 15–18 classification problems

#### Step 2.3: Model Evaluation & Selection
- Train/validation/test splits
- Cross-validation (k-fold, stratified)
- Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, confusion matrix
- Hyperparameter tuning: GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV
- **Practice tasks:** 12–15 evaluation/tuning problems

---

### **Phase 3: Unsupervised Learning (Week 6)**

#### Step 3.1: Clustering
- K-means: centroid-based clustering, elbow method
- Hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN
- Evaluation: silhouette score, inertia
- **Practice tasks:** 8–10 clustering problems

#### Step 3.2: Dimensionality Reduction
- Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
- Feature selection vs. feature extraction
- Visualization in 2D/3D
- **Practice tasks:** 6–8 dimensionality reduction problems

---

### **Phase 4: Deep Learning Fundamentals with TensorFlow (Weeks 7–9)**

#### Step 4.1: Neural Network Basics
- Perceptrons, layers, neurons, weights, biases
- Activation functions: ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax
- Forward propagation and backpropagation concepts
- Loss functions: MSE (regression), cross-entropy (classification)
- Optimizers: SGD, Adam, RMSprop
- **Practice tasks:** 10–12 neural network foundation problems

#### Step 4.2: Building & Training Models with Keras
- Sequential API: stacking layers with `Dense`, `Dropout`, `BatchNormalization`
- Functional API: building complex architectures
- Compilation: loss, optimizer, metrics
- Fitting and validation
- Callbacks: EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint
- **Practice tasks:** 15–18 Keras model building problems

#### Step 4.3: Preventing Overfitting
- Dropout layers
- L1/L2 regularization
- Batch normalization
- Data augmentation
- **Practice tasks:** 8–10 regularization problems

---

### **Phase 5: Specialized Architectures (Weeks 10–11)**

#### Step 5.1: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
- Conv2D layers, kernel sizes, padding, stride
- MaxPooling, AvgPooling
- Building image classifiers for MNIST, CIFAR-10
- Transfer learning: pre-trained models (ResNet, VGG, Inception)
- Fine-tuning strategies
- **Practice tasks:** 12–15 CNN problems

#### Step 5.2: Recurrent Neural Networks & LSTMs
- LSTM cells vs. vanilla RNNs
- Sequences, timesteps, return_sequences
- Bidirectional LSTMs
- Time series forecasting, sentiment classification
- Encoder-Decoder architectures (intro)
- **Practice tasks:** 10–12 RNN/LSTM problems

---

### **Phase 6: Integration & Real-World Practice (Week 12)**

#### Step 6.1: End-to-End ML Projects
- Complete pipeline: data → preprocessing → model → evaluation → tuning
- Combining Sklearn + TensorFlow in a single project
- Saving and loading models (`joblib` for Sklearn, `model.save()` for TensorFlow)
- **Practice tasks:** 5–8 full-stack projects

#### Step 6.2: Interview Simulation
- Timed coding challenges on ML problems
- Explaining model choices and tradeoffs
- Debugging underperforming models
- **Practice tasks:** 5–7 interview-style scenarios

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Technical Competencies**

1. **Data Manipulation & Preprocessing**
   - Imputation, normalization, encoding, feature engineering
   - Detecting and handling class imbalance
   - Creating train/validation/test splits

2. **Algorithm Implementation**
   - Instantiate, fit, and tune 10+ Sklearn models
   - Understand hyperparameter effects and relationships
   - Know when to choose each algorithm

3. **Neural Network Design**
   - Design architectures for different problem types (tabular, image, sequence)
   - Tune learning rates, batch sizes, layer depths
   - Diagnose overfitting and apply remedies

4. **Evaluation & Diagnosis**
   - Select appropriate metrics for your problem
   - Interpret confusion matrices, ROC curves, precision-recall trade-offs
   - Perform ablation studies and feature importance analysis

5. **Production Considerations**
   - Model serialization and versioning
   - Inference time optimization
   - Handling edge cases and data drift
